pr_title: CultureInfo and CultureData use OS information to initialize culture routines on Windows
pr_body:
Fixes: #35638 

ICU doesn't use OS data to get the default user settings in Windows for current culture, current UI culture and for current region.

cc: @tarekgh @jkotas @GrabYourPitchforks @jefgen
pr_comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @tarekgh, @safern, @krwq
Notify danmosemsft if you want to be subscribed.

> ICU doesn't use OS data to get the default user settings in Windows for current culture, current UI culture and for current region.

Can you explain what you mean by this?

ICU on Windows *should* be picking up the NLS User Locale setting, often called the "Regional Format" setting. If this isn't happening then there's a serious bug going on.

For example, this is what the UI for the setting looks like in the Settings App on Windows 10:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29107334/80763336-2a532700-8af3-11ea-9200-a3181224f3c8.png)
@jefgen does ICU on Windows offer returning the Default UI language and default Region too?

@jefgen thanks. 

This change is mainly to get the default user and UI language and default region. We'll need to use NLS anyway for UI and Region, then I would say it doesn't matter if we use NLS for user locale too. so @safern changes here is reasonable to me.

Sure, that sounds reasonable to me.
I just wanted to make sure that there wasn't some kind of horrible bug here with ICU, as when I read this part:
> ICU doesn't use OS data to get the default user settings in Windows

I was concerned that maybe there was a bug and the ICU wasn't reading the NLS User Default Locale (which it should be).

Thanks for the replies and clarifications. :)
Build is green, GH just didn't update.

issue_context.title: Problem with UI Culture
issue_context.body:
I think i need an explanation about why NlsGetUserDefaultUICulture uses InitializeUserDefaultCulture instead of InitializeUserDefaultUICulture. I think this is why i get the wrong result when using CurrentUICulture when my process is running as system.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1db45ed953745c0e270d09df99828cb58772f4ad/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/CultureInfo.Nls.cs#L82
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @tarekgh, @safern, @krwq
Notify danmosemsft if you want to be subscribed.

InitializeUserDefaultUICulture is calling NlsGetUserDefaultUICulture. We cannot make NlsGetUserDefaultUICulture to call InitializeUserDefaultUICulture or it will be infinite loop.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1db45ed953745c0e270d09df99828cb58772f4ad/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/CultureInfo.cs#L826

could you tell me more about your environment to investigate? we may have some bug somewhere. Are you turning Nls config switch on? otherwise, you'll be using ICU by default now which maybe the bug in this path. 

CC @safern

I think the bug is here 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1db45ed953745c0e270d09df99828cb58772f4ad/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/CultureInfo.Icu.cs#L45
thanks @Robert-LTH for reporting this issue. we'll try to fix this soon.

Thank you for looking into this! I can add some info to this, it might help you understand my issue.

if i run `dism /online /get-intl` it outputs

> Default system UI language : en-US

Default User Locale is sv-SE.

If i check the properties of `CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture` it has LCID = 1053 (sv-SE). I expect this to be 1033 (en-US).

@Robert-LTH thanks for the info. I assume you are using v5.0 bits here as the whole discussion around that. Just to ensure we all in the same page. 

As a workaround, if this is blocking you, you may use the config switch https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/dd22ce809f235b40f20737b56458bacdb8ec2b46/src/libraries/System.Globalization/tests/NlsTests/runtimeconfig.template.json#L3.
Thanks @Robert-LTH for reporting the issue. I've put up a PR to fix this: #35680

review_comments:
Unrelated to the change at hand, but does this just take the NLS alternate sort names and blindly tack them after the "`@collation`" keyword? 

If so, then FWIW, this won't work as the NLS alternate sort names do not match the ICU keywords.

For example:
In NLS you'll have "`de-DE_phoneb`", but with ICU this would need to be "`de-DE@collation=phonebook`" or "`de-DE-u-co-phonebk`"

Same remark on the ICU->NLS side as well I think.
(You'll end up with `de-DE_phonebook` when you probably wanted `de-DE_phoneb`).

Isn't the user is passing us the name? this is not conversion between Nls and ICU. This is just normalizing the locale name to make it work with ICU. We'll just respect whatever the user giving us. 

The question is, if anyone want to use a locale name that can work on Windows(NLS) and ICU, what name they should use? we can ty to help in converting the alternatesortname but I am seeing this can cause other problems as users will get something different than what they passed to us. what you think about that?

---
In reply to: [418672754](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/35680#discussion_r418672754) [](ancestors = 418672754)

So it seems like in this case we will endup with `de-DE@collation=phoneb` for ICU:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/9351765ba806a40b4da4bfae876c8f398a6ffc97/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/CultureData.cs#L870

That calls into: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1db45ed953745c0e270d09df99828cb58772f4ad/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/CultureData.Icu.cs#L312

Which would return: 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1db45ed953745c0e270d09df99828cb58772f4ad/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/IcuLocaleData.cs#L4440-L4442

And that returns: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1db45ed953745c0e270d09df99828cb58772f4ad/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/IcuLocaleData.cs#L154

NLS scenario PInvokes to get the local name  from the locale id so I get we're fine on NLS: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f185bd5571f2500b4843d145418c4418747246b6/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/CultureData.Nls.cs#L610

cc: @tarekgh am I following this correct?
@safern this is not about mapping LCID to culture name.

>Isn't the user is passing us the name? this is not conversion between Nls and ICU. This is just normalizing the locale name to make it work with ICU

Well in that case why bother handling the `_` (alt sort) at all then? If this is just taking the user input then I guess it's up to them to give the correct input I suppose? 
If the intent isn't to convert between NLS and ICU at all, then perhaps maybe add a comment to that effect -- as the code is somewhat confusing (at least to me seeing this for the first time). :)

Reading a comment like this:
`// Replace _ (alternate sort) with @collation= for ICU`
and then seeing a bunch of code that alters/manipulates the input locale name gives the impression that you're trying to do at least *some* kind of mapping from the given input to an ICU style locale name.

> if anyone want to use a locale name that can work on Windows(NLS) and ICU, what name they should use?

I'd probably suggest using a BCP47 language tag like this: "`de-DE-u-co-phonebk`", though at least for Windows(NLS) that would only work on Windows 10, and not down-level, so its not a great solution.

> but I am seeing this can cause other problems as users will get something different than what they passed to us. 

Yes, that's a fair point. I don't know what the expectation is w.r.t. altering the given input tags at all.

> Well in that case why bother handling the _ (alt sort) at all then? If this is just taking the user input then I guess it's up to them to give the correct input I suppose?

.NET doesn't support ICU naming convention. Users have to give the expected form of locale names. We used the original Windows convention for naming when using alternative sort (i.e. `_`). To call ICU, we'll have to normalize the name to the form that ICU can work nicely with. that is why we do this normalization.

> I'd probably suggest using a BCP47 language tag like this: "de-DE-u-co-phonebk", though at least for Windows(NLS) that would only work on Windows 10, and not down-level, so its not a great solution.

This will not work on downlevel as you pointed out.

Anyways, my intent was not to derail this PR with unrelated issues... :)

This was mostly just wanting to point something out that I noticed while looking at the change. I was somewhat surprised to see this kind of manipulation of locale tags, and I (mistakenly) thought the code was trying to do some kind of mapping here, and getting it wrong, so I wanted to try to help out by pointing it out. It might be worth discussing this offline later on I suppose.
@jefgen your feedback is always valuable and adds something to our knowledge. keep doing that :-). We can discuss that offline as you suggested.

Thanks @tarekgh. :-)

One last comment I suppose...
> We used the original Windows convention for naming when using alternative sort (i.e. _).

Hmm, well if this is the case (using Windows-style naming), then *maybe* you might want to consider some kind of basic mapping of the names? (In order to have `de-DE_phoneb` input still give phonebook sort order).
But then again, I'm not sure if this is perhaps needed at all, given this:
> Users have to give the expected form of locale names.

So maybe this is a broader question of expectations/documentation on what sorts of input tags should be used, etc.

> then maybe you might want to consider some kind of basic mapping of the names?

We may consider that as long as we are not changing the name that the user passed to us. I mean CultureInfo.Name property will match the name that user passed to us. I think this will be reasonable to do. does the phonebook sorting name is the only case here or we have more cases like that?
